topics: Data Analysis and Statistics for AI

questions.q: What is the median of the dataset 3, 9, 4, 7, 12?
questions.x: Sort the values (3, 4, 7, 9, 12); the middle value is 7.

questions.q: Variance is calculated as the average of the:
o: differences between the largest and smallest values
questions.x: Variance averages the squared deviations of each value from the mean.

questions.q: What is the range of the dataset 14, 3, 22, 9, 17?
questions.x: Range = maximum − minimum = 22 − 3 = 19.

questions.q: A game pays $10 with probability 0.2 and $0 otherwise. What is the expected value of one play?
questions.x: Expected value = 10 × 0.2 + 0 × 0.8 = $2.

questions.q: If every value in a dataset is increased by 5, what happens to the standard deviation?
questions.x: Adding a constant shifts the data but does not change its spread.

questions.q: The number of customers who enter a store each hour is an example of which type of variable?
questions.x: Counts take whole-number values, so they are discrete.

questions.q: A z-score of 2.0 means a value is:
o: twice as large as the mean
two standard deviations above the mean
questions.x: A z-score measures distance from the mean in standard deviations.

questions.q: Which statistic indicates whether two variables tend to increase or decrease together?
o: Standard error of a single variable
questions.x: Covariance is positive when two variables move together and negative when they move in opposite directions.

questions.q: Which of the following is most affected by extreme outliers?
questions.x: The mean uses every value, so a single extreme value can pull it significantly; the median is resistant.

questions.q: What is the mean of 4, 8, 6, 10, and 2?
questions.x: The sum is 30 and there are 5 values, so the mean is 30 / 5 = 6.

questions.q: Which measure describes how far, on average, data values fall from the mean, in the same units as the data?
questions.x: Standard deviation is the square root of variance, so it is expressed in the original units of the data.

questions.q: In a normal (Gaussian) distribution, approximately what percentage of values fall within one standard deviation of the mean?
questions.x: The empirical rule: about 68% within 1 SD, 95% within 2 SD, and 99.7% within 3 SD.

questions.q: The probability of an event that is certain to happen is:
questions.x: Probabilities range from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).

questions.q: Which type of variable takes values such as 'red,' 'blue,' and 'green' with no natural order?
questions.x: Nominal variables are categories without a ranking.

questions.q: A person's height measured in centimeters is an example of a:
questions.x: Height can take any value within a range, so it is continuous.

questions.q: A fair six-sided die is rolled once. What is the expected value of the roll?
A dataset contains the values 5, 5, 6, 8, 9, 5, 10. What is the mode?
questions.x: The mode is the value that appears most often; 5 appears three times.

questions.q: Which statement describes a Gaussian (normal) distribution?
o: Its values are evenly spread across a fixed range
It is symmetric and bell-shaped, with mean, median, and mode equal
It is always skewed to the right
questions.x: A normal distribution is a symmetric bell curve centered on the mean, where mean = median = mode.

questions.q: A decision tree makes predictions by:
o: drawing a single straight line through the data
splitting data on feature values through a series of if-then branches
questions.x: Each internal node tests a feature, and each leaf gives a prediction.

questions.q: Outliers in a boxplot are usually shown as:
questions.x: Points beyond about 1.5 × IQR from the box are plotted individually as potential outliers.

questions.q: Which visualization would best compare total sales across five store locations?
questions.x: Bar charts compare values across distinct categories.

questions.q: A pie chart is most appropriate when you want to show:
o: parts of a whole that add up to 100%
the relationship between two continuous variables
questions.x: Pie charts compare category shares of a single total.

questions.q: K-means is an algorithm used for:
o: grouping similar data points into clusters
questions.x: K-means is an unsupervised method that partitions data into k clusters around centroids.

questions.q: Which chart shows the distribution of a single numerical variable by grouping values into bins?
questions.x: A histogram uses adjacent bars to show how many values fall into each range (bin).

questions.q: Multiple linear regression differs from simple linear regression because it:
o: uses two or more independent variables
questions.x: Simple regression has one predictor; multiple regression uses several.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common data quality problem?
o: Storing data in a relational database
questions.x: Duplicates, missing values, inconsistent formats, and low-quality sources all reduce data quality.

questions.q: Dependence methods in multivariate analysis are used when:
o: the data has only one variable
all variables are treated equally with no outcome variable
one or more variables are predicted from other variables
questions.x: Dependence methods (e.g., regression) have dependent and independent variables; interdependence methods (e.g., cluster or factor analysis) look for structure among all variables.

questions.q: Correlation between two variables does NOT prove that:
o: a scatterplot would show a pattern
questions.x: Correlation does not imply causation; a third factor may influence both.

questions.q: Using a biased, low-quality source to collect data most likely leads to:
questions.x: Data quality depends on reliable sources; biased data produces biased results.

questions.q: Why is data cleaning an important step before building a model?
o: It replaces the need to test the model
Errors, duplicates, and missing values can lead to inaccurate results
It is required only for unstructured data
questions.x: 'Garbage in, garbage out': models trained on messy data produce unreliable predictions.

questions.q: A survey dataset is missing answers for 30% of respondents on one question. This is an example of:
questions.x: Missing values make a dataset incomplete and can bias results.

questions.q: A boxplot displays which set of values?
o: Each individual data point in time order
Minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, and maximum
questions.x: The box spans Q1 to Q3 with a line at the median; whiskers extend toward the min and max (outliers are often plotted separately).

questions.q: Logistic regression is typically used to predict:
o: a categorical outcome, such as yes/no
the number of clusters in data
questions.x: Logistic regression outputs a probability for class membership (e.g., will a customer churn: yes or no).

questions.q: An analyst notices that 'NY,' 'New York,' and 'new york' all appear in a state column. What is the best cleaning step?
o: Standardize the values into one consistent format
Convert the column to a histogram
Ignore it because it does not matter
questions.x: Inconsistent labels split one category into several; standardizing fixes the error.

questions.q: Which chart is best for showing the relationship between two numerical variables, such as advertising spend and sales?
questions.x: Scatterplots place each observation on two numeric axes, making correlation visible.

questions.q: Which is an interdependence technique for multivariate data?
o: Analysis of a single variable's mean
questions.x: Interdependence methods examine relationships among variables without designating an outcome.

questions.q: Which visual is most appropriate for showing a company's monthly revenue over two years?
questions.x: Line charts show trends over time.

questions.q: Which algorithm predicts a continuous numeric value, such as a home price, from one or more input variables using a best-fit line?
questions.x: Linear regression models a numeric outcome as a linear function of inputs.

questions.q: R is a programming language especially popular for:
questions.x: R was designed for statistics and has strong visualization packages such as ggplot2.

questions.q: In a relational database, a primary key is a field that:
o: uniquely identifies each record in a table
questions.x: Each row must have a unique, non-null primary key value.

questions.q: PyTorch is a library mainly used to:
o: build and train deep learning models
questions.x: PyTorch is an open-source deep learning framework.

questions.q: Which SQL clause filters rows based on a condition?
questions.x: WHERE limits results to rows that meet a condition, e.g., WHERE state = 'PA'.

questions.q: Which SQL keyword combines rows from two tables based on a related column?
questions.x: JOIN (INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL) matches rows on related keys.

questions.q: Which Python library is widely used for working with tabular data in DataFrames?
questions.x: Pandas provides DataFrame and Series structures for cleaning and analyzing tabular data.

questions.q: NumPy is primarily used in Python for:
questions.x: NumPy provides efficient n-dimensional arrays and mathematical functions.

questions.q: Which SQL statement retrieves data from a table?
questions.x: SELECT queries return rows and columns from one or more tables.

questions.q: In Pandas, the function commonly used to remove rows with missing values is:
questions.x: dropna() removes rows (or columns) containing missing values; fillna() replaces them instead.

questions.q: Which SQL clause sorts query results?
questions.x: ORDER BY sorts results ascending (ASC, default) or descending (DESC).

questions.q: Which SQL query returns all columns from a table named Customers?
questions.x: The asterisk selects every column.

questions.q: Relational databases organize data into:
o: tables of rows and columns connected by keys
questions.x: Tables relate to one another through primary and foreign keys.

questions.q: A large language model (LLM) is:
o: an AI model trained on very large amounts of text to understand and generate language
questions.x: LLMs learn statistical patterns in text and generate language one token at a time.

questions.q: Which task is an LLM generally well suited for?
o: Guaranteeing that every fact it states is true
questions.x: LLMs are strong at language tasks like summarization, but outputs must be verified.

questions.q: Natural language processing (NLP) enables computers to:
questions.x: NLP covers tasks such as translation, summarization, and chatbots.

questions.q: A chatbot answering customer questions in plain language is an application of:
questions.x: Understanding and responding in language is NLP.

questions.q: Which is an example of generative AI used in healthcare?
o: Drafting clinical notes or summarizing patient records
questions.x: Generative AI can draft and summarize text, with clinicians reviewing it.

questions.q: Which AI subfield focuses on enabling computers to interpret images and video?
questions.x: Computer vision deals with understanding visual input.

questions.q: Which is a known limitation of generative AI?
o: It can produce confident but incorrect information
questions.x: Generative models can 'hallucinate' plausible-sounding but false content.

questions.q: Robotics as an AI subfield is primarily concerned with:
o: machines that sense and act in the physical world
questions.x: Robotics combines perception, planning, and control for physical agents.

questions.q: Image generators that create artwork from a text prompt are an example of:
questions.x: They generate new images based on patterns learned from training data.

questions.q: Artificial intelligence is best defined as:
o: computer systems performing tasks that typically require human intelligence
the physical parts of a computer
any computer with a fast processor
questions.x: AI includes reasoning, learning, perception, and language understanding by machines.

questions.q: The text an LLM is given as input to produce a response is called a:
questions.x: Users guide model output through prompts.

questions.q: Generative AI refers to systems that:
o: only sort existing data into categories
create new content such as text, images, or audio
questions.x: Generative models produce new content that resembles their training data.

questions.q: A model that performs very well on training data but poorly on new data is said to be:
questions.x: Overfitting means the model memorized noise rather than learning general patterns.

questions.q: Which machine learning approach is most appropriate for predicting whether an email is spam using thousands of emails already labeled spam or not spam?
questions.x: Labeled examples and a categorical target make this a supervised classification problem.

questions.q: Why is a separate test dataset used after training a model?
o: To store backup copies of data
To evaluate how well the model performs on data it has not seen
questions.x: Testing on unseen data estimates real-world performance.

questions.q: An artificial neural network is made up of connected units called:
questions.x: Inputs pass through layers of weighted nodes to produce outputs.

questions.q: Supervised learning uses:
o: labeled data with known correct outputs
questions.x: Each training example includes the correct answer (label).

questions.q: Training a robot to walk by trial and error with rewards for staying upright is an example of:
questions.x: The robot learns from feedback on its actions.

questions.q: Deep learning uses:
questions.x: 'Deep' refers to many layers of artificial neurons that learn features automatically.

questions.q: During training, a neural network adjusts its internal parameters, called:
questions.x: Weights are updated (e.g., by backpropagation) to reduce prediction error.

questions.q: The validation dataset is commonly used to:
o: tune model settings and choose between models during development
questions.x: Validation data guides hyperparameter tuning; the test set gives the final unbiased evaluation.

questions.q: Machine learning is a branch of AI in which systems:
o: learn patterns from data rather than following only hand-written rules
are programmed with every possible answer
questions.x: ML models improve performance on a task as they learn from examples.

questions.q: Reinforcement learning trains an agent by:
o: rewarding desirable actions and penalizing undesirable ones
providing labeled examples for every input
questions.x: The agent learns a policy that maximizes cumulative reward, e.g., game-playing AI.

questions.q: Grouping customers into segments without predefined labels is an example of:
questions.x: Unsupervised learning finds structure such as clusters in unlabeled data.

questions.q: Knowledge representation and reasoning (KR&R) in AI is concerned with:
o: storing information about the world in a form a computer can use to draw conclusions
questions.x: KR&R uses structures such as logic, rules, ontologies, and semantic networks.

questions.q: How does probability-based reasoning differ from logic-based reasoning?
o: It handles uncertainty by assigning likelihoods instead of only true/false values
questions.x: Logic deals with definite truth values; probabilistic reasoning quantifies uncertainty.

questions.q: The 'perception' component of an AI system involves:
o: gathering and interpreting input from sensors such as cameras or microphones
questions.x: Perception turns raw sensory data into usable information.

questions.q: The symbol ∃ in predicate logic means:
questions.x: ∃ is the existential quantifier; ∀ is the universal quantifier.

questions.q: In a Bayesian network, the nodes represent:
questions.x: Each node is a variable with a conditional probability table.

questions.q: Bayesian networks must be directed acyclic graphs, which means:
o: every node connects to every other node
edges have direction and there are no cycles
the graph loops back on itself
questions.x: Acyclic means you cannot follow arrows and return to the same node.

questions.q: In a Bayesian network, the edges represent:
questions.x: A directed edge from A to B indicates that B depends on A.

questions.q: Which statement is an example of probabilistic reasoning?
o: There is a 70% chance of rain given the current conditions
If A then B; A; therefore B
questions.x: It expresses a likelihood rather than a certain truth.

questions.q: Predicate logic represents knowledge using:
o: predicates, variables, and quantifiers such as 'for all' and 'there exists'
questions.x: Example: ∀x (Human(x) → Mortal(x)).

questions.q: An expert system that uses rules such as 'IF fever AND cough THEN possible flu' is an example of:
questions.x: Expert systems apply if-then rules to a knowledge base.

questions.q: Which is an example of a statement in predicate logic?
questions.x: It means 'for every x, if x is a dog, then x is an animal.'

questions.q: A Bayesian network is a model that represents:
o: variables and their probabilistic dependencies as a directed acyclic graph
questions.x: Nodes are variables; directed edges show conditional dependencies.

questions.q: Deepfakes created with generative AI are a concern because they can:
o: spread convincing misinformation by imitating real people
questions.x: Realistic fake audio or video can deceive viewers.

questions.q: An LLM confidently stating a fact that is false is known as a:
questions.x: Hallucinations are fabricated outputs presented as true.

questions.q: A self-driving car must choose between two harmful outcomes in an unavoidable crash. This raises an:
questions.x: Autonomous vehicles raise questions about how machines should make moral decisions.

questions.q: Algorithmic bias in AI most often comes from:
questions.x: Models learn patterns in their data, including historical biases.

questions.q: Facial recognition used for mass public surveillance raises concerns mainly about:
questions.x: Constant identification of people in public can threaten privacy and enable misuse.

questions.q: Before sharing a statistic produced by a chatbot, the best practice is to:
o: verify it with a reliable source
questions.x: LLM output can contain misinformation and should be fact-checked.

questions.q: Transparency in AI systems means:
o: people can understand how and why the system makes decisions
the code is deleted after use
questions.x: Explainability builds trust and makes it easier to find errors and bias.

questions.q: A hiring algorithm trained on past hiring decisions that favored one gender may:
o: repeat that bias in its recommendations
questions.x: Models inherit patterns, including discrimination, from historical data.

questions.q: Which is an intellectual property concern with generative AI?
o: Generated content may closely copy copyrighted training material
questions.x: Questions remain about training on and reproducing copyrighted works.

questions.q: A 'prompt injection' attack against an LLM application attempts to:
o: trick the model into ignoring its instructions or revealing data
questions.x: Malicious inputs can manipulate model behavior, a security risk for LLM apps.

questions.q: Which practice helps reduce bias in an AI hiring tool?
o: Hiding how the model makes decisions
Using only data from one demographic group
Training on diverse, representative data and auditing outcomes across groups
questions.x: Representative data and regular fairness audits help detect and reduce bias.

questions.q: Which is a privacy risk associated with using LLMs?
o: Users may enter sensitive personal data that is stored or exposed
questions.x: Sensitive data typed into prompts may be logged, retained, or leaked.

questions.q: What is the hexadecimal representation of the decimal number 255?
Data collected by a fitness tracker, such as step counts and heart rate, is an example of data gathered from:
questions.x: Wearables and IoT devices continuously generate sensor data.

questions.q: Which is an example of unstructured data?
o: A table of order numbers and dates
A list of product prices in a database
questions.x: Unstructured data lacks a predefined tabular format.

questions.q: Data wrangling refers to:
o: cleaning, restructuring, and transforming raw data into a usable format
questions.x: Wrangling prepares messy raw data for analysis.

questions.q: Which representation is commonly used to write colors in web design, such as #FF5733?
questions.x: Hex color codes give red, green, and blue values from 00 to FF.

questions.q: Which is typically the first stage of the data science process?
questions.x: A clear question guides what data to collect and how to analyze it.

questions.q: Why is exploratory data analysis (EDA) performed?
o: To summarize the data's main characteristics and spot patterns or problems before modeling
questions.x: EDA uses statistics and charts to understand data first.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'big data'?
o: Datasets so large, fast, or varied that traditional tools struggle to process them
Data printed in a large font
Any spreadsheet with more than 10 rows
questions.x: Big data is often described by volume, velocity, and variety.

questions.q: Data science combines which fields to extract insight from data?
o: Statistics, computer science, and domain knowledge
questions.x: Data scientists use math/statistics, programming, and subject expertise.

questions.q: Semi-structured data, such as JSON or XML files, is best described as data that:
o: is always stored in relational tables
has tags or keys for organization but not a rigid table schema
questions.x: JSON/XML include labels that organize data without fixed rows and columns.

questions.q: Ordinal data differs from nominal data because ordinal data:
o: has a meaningful order, such as small/medium/large
questions.x: Ordinal categories can be ranked; nominal categories cannot.

questions.q: Which is an example of structured data?
o: A collection of social media videos
A spreadsheet of customer names, IDs, and purchase totals
questions.x: Structured data fits a predefined schema of rows and columns.

questions.q: What is the binary representation of the decimal number 13?
Normalizing a numeric feature to a 0–1 range is done to:
o: put features on a comparable scale
questions.x: Scaling keeps features with large ranges from dominating some algorithms.

questions.q: How many different values can be represented with 8 bits?
What is the decimal value of the binary number 1010?
Which sequence best represents the data science process?
o: Model data, define problem, delete data, collect data
Communicate results, collect data, define the problem, clean data
Define the problem, collect data, clean data, explore and model, communicate results
Clean data, publish, define problem, collect data
questions.x: The process moves from question to data to analysis to communication (often iteratively).

questions.q: Which of the following is numeric data?
o: The number of items in a shopping cart
questions.x: Numeric data represents measurable quantities.

questions.q: Converting a 'date of birth' column into an 'age' column is an example of:
questions.x: Transformation creates more useful features from existing data.

questions.q: Which of the following is a categorical data point?
questions.x: Categorical data describes groups or labels rather than measured quantities.

questions.q: Which data source would provide data about public opinion on a new product?
questions.x: Opinions are captured in surveys, reviews, and social posts.

questions.q: What is the decimal value of the hexadecimal number 1F?
